public.text: The AI-readiness and trustworthy-AI sections cover evidence, human oversight, accountability and periodic evaluation. What is less clear is how a deployed AI capability should connect to routine clinical governance, incident reporting and service management. Making that connection explicit would help ensure that model monitoring is considered alongside care outcomes and frontline signals.
public.suggestedRevision: Add lifecycle requirements for locally representative clinical validation; a named clinical owner; workflow and human-factors assessment; logging and traceability; subgroup performance and drift monitoring; accessible clinician override and incident-reporting routes; and predefined criteria for restriction, rollback or suspension. Require these signals to feed existing clinical-governance and patient-safety systems, not a parallel AI-only process.
